During a longitudinal study participant drop-out poses a significant risk; this will 
be mitigated via the regular interviews and A/B testing focusing on features to 
enhance student retention rates. Data privacy, like with this projects conducted 
study, is of paramount concern particularly when it comes to the collection and 
handling of personal data. GDPR, privacy laws, along with clear communication 
with participants on how their data will be handled, ensures the study remains 
ethical and respects the participants. 
5.9 Implemented Features and Performance Testing 
The implementation of the project plan using a hybrid methodology with 
waterfall and agile, has culminated to be a significant success. The project 
exhibited some challenges such as finding a tutor to conduct the study, however 
the planned-in redundancy periods helped mitigate these issues. The project was 
developed up to and including task 40; by which time the deadline to finish 
working on the project had come to pass. This highlights a short coming when 
planning the project that more time was needed. Despite this the project has 
completed well into the COULD haves from the functional requirements, and has 
implemented all of the non-functional requirements.  
To test the applications performance for the non-functional requirements, JMeter 
was utilised, with 10 threads sending an unlimited number of messages per 
second. The application did not produce any error responses, and was able to 
handle a maximum of 163 messages per second. Results can be found in 
Appendix A, JMeter Readings.
